answer: ORAL Surveillance trial showed higher risks of MACE and cancers with tofacitinib compared to TNF inhibitors in a cardiovascular risk-enriched RA population. STAR-RA study found no increased cardiovascular risk with tofacitinib in real-world RA patients but a non-significant increased risk in those with cardiovascular risk factors. STAR-RA included two cohorts: a real-world evidence cohort and an RCT-duplicate cohort mimicking ORAL Surveillance criteria to calibrate findings. FDA requires new warnings about increased risk of major adverse cardiovascular events, malignancy, thrombosis, and mortality with tofacitinib and other JAK inhibitors. FDA's ORAL Surveillance trial required patients ≥50 years with ≥1 cardiovascular risk factor, comparing tofacitinib 5 mg and 10 mg twice daily to TNF blockers, with MACE and malignancy as co-primary endpoints. Xeljanz prescribing information states RA Safety Study 1 showed higher rates of MACE and mortality with tofacitinib 5 mg and 10 mg twice daily versus TNF blockers in RA patients ≥50 years with cardiovascular risk factors. The label notes the non-inferiority criterion was not met in RA Safety Study 1; increased risks of death, MACE, malignancies, serious infections, and thromboembolic events were observed with tofacitinib. ORAL Surveillance showed increased cardiovascular risk with tofacitinib in high-risk RA patients, while STAR-RA real-world data did not find significant risk overall; FDA warnings and label reflect ORAL Surveillance findings, highlighting uncertainties in risk magnitude and patient subgroups.
